question_html: Which section of the Companies Act, 2013 governs the issue and redemption of preference shares?

options.A: Section 52
options.B: Section 53
options.C: Section 55
options.D: Section 63

answer_html: Answer: (C) In India, the issue and redemption of preference shares is governed by Section 55 of the Companies Act, 2013[cite: 15].

question_html: What is the maximum period within which preference shares are required to be redeemed under the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: 10 years
options.B: 15 years
options.C: 20 years
options.D: 30 years

answer_html: Answer: (C) Preference shares are liable to be redeemed within a period normally not exceeding 20 years from the date of their issue[cite: 15].

question_html: Can a company issue irredeemable preference shares under the current company law framework in India?

options.A: Yes, if authorized by the Articles of Association.
options.B: No, a company cannot issue irredeemable preference shares[cite: 15].
options.C: Yes, with the prior approval of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT).
options.D: Yes, if they are fully paid up within 5 years.

answer_html: Answer: (B) A company cannot issue irredeemable preference shares under the Companies Act, 2013[cite: 15].

question_html: Under Section 55, out of which funds can redeemable preference shares be redeemed?

options.A: Out of any reserves including revaluation reserve.
options.B: Out of divisible profits or out of the proceeds of a fresh issue of shares made for the purpose[cite: 15].
options.C: Out of the proceeds of debentures or fixed deposits.
options.D: Out of capital reserve or securities premium.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Shares can only be redeemed out of divisible profits or out of proceeds of a fresh issue of shares made for that purpose[cite: 15].

question_html: What is the legal prerequisite regarding the paid-up status of preference shares before they can be redeemed?

options.A: They can be partly paid-up if the board approves.
options.B: They must be fully paid-up[cite: 15].
options.C: At least 50% must be paid-up.
options.D: Call-in-arrears up to 10% is permissible for redemption.

answer_html: Answer: (B) No preference shares can be redeemed unless they are fully paid-up[cite: 15].

question_html: What is the primary purpose behind the creation of the Capital Redemption Reserve (CRR) Account?

options.A: To write off preliminary expenses and discount on shares.
options.B: To protect the interest of creditors and outsiders by maintaining the same amount of shareholders' funds[cite: 15].
options.C: To distribute tax-free cash dividends to equity shareholders.
options.D: To pay the premium on redemption of debentures.

answer_html: Answer: (B) CRR ensures that the security for creditors/bankers is not reduced upon redemption of capital out of profits[cite: 15].

question_html: To what exclusive use is the Capital Redemption Reserve (CRR) Account restricted under the Companies Act, 2013?

options.A: Writing off capital losses
options.B: Issuance of fully paid-up bonus shares only[cite: 15]
options.C: Payment of preference dividends
options.D: Buyback of equity shares

answer_html: Answer: (B) The utilisation of CRR Account is restricted to the issuance of fully paid-up bonus shares only[cite: 15].

question_html: For companies whose financial statements comply with Accounting Standards under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013, can the securities premium account be utilized to provide for the premium payable on redemption of preference shares?

options.A: Yes, always.
options.B: No, such companies cannot apply the securities premium account for premium on redemption of preference shares[cite: 15].
options.C: Yes, if approved by a special resolution.
options.D: Only if capital redemption reserve is insufficient.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Companies complying with Section 133 and AS cannot apply securities premium for writing off premium on redemption[cite: 15].
topic_text: Securities Premium and Redemption Premium under Section 133

question_html: Can the proceeds from the issue of debentures be utilized for the redemption of preference shares?

options.A: Yes, if they are secured debentures.
options.B: No, proceeds from the issue of debentures cannot be utilised for preference share redemption[cite: 15].
options.C: Yes, with Reserve Bank of India approval.
options.D: Yes, up to 50% of the redemption value.

answer_html: Answer: (B) The proceeds from the issue of debentures cannot be utilised for the purpose of preference share redemption[cite: 15].

question_html: How is preference dividend treated in accounts when a company incurs a net loss during a financial year?

options.A: Treated as a charge against profits and payable regardless of loss.
options.B: Treated as an appropriation of profits and not payable if there is no profit[cite: 15].
options.C: Converted automatically into debenture interest.
options.D: Paid out of share capital.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Preference dividend declared/paid continues to be regarded as an appropriation of profits, unlike debenture interest which is a charge[cite: 15].

question_html: S Ltd. issued 2,000, 10% Preference shares of ₹100 each at par on 1.4.2022, redeemable at 10% premium. The company issued 1,500 Equity Shares of ₹100 each at 20% premium for redemption. What amount is transferred to CRR?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Face value of preference shares redeemed = ₹2,00,000. Less face value of fresh equity shares issued = ₹1,50,000. Amount to CRR = ₹2,00,000 - ₹1,50,000 = ₹50,000[cite: 15].

question_html: Preference shares amounting to ₹2,00,000 are redeemed at 5% premium by issuing shares worth ₹1,00,000 at 10% premium. What is the amount to be transferred to Capital Redemption Reserve?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Face value of shares redeemed (₹2,00,000) minus face value of fresh issue (₹1,00,000) = ₹1,00,000[cite: 15].

question_html: Which of the following accounts CANNOT be used for the creation of a Capital Redemption Reserve Account?

options.A: General Reserve Account
options.B: Profit and Loss Account (Credit Balance)
options.C: Unclaimed Dividend Account[cite: 15]
options.D: Dividend Equalisation Reserve

answer_html: Answer: (C) Unclaimed dividend is a current liability, not a divisible profit, hence it cannot be used to create CRR[cite: 15].

question_html: According to Section 52 of the Companies Act, 2013, the amount in the Securities Premium Account CANNOT be used for which of the following?

options.A: Issue of fully paid bonus shares
options.B: Writing off trading losses of the company[cite: 15]
options.C: Purchase of its own shares or other securities
options.D: Writing off preliminary expenses of the company

answer_html: Answer: (B) Securities premium cannot be used for writing off general trading losses[cite: 15].

question_html: What is the correct accounting treatment when preference shares are redeemed at par?

options.A: Debit Redeemable Preference Share Capital A/c, Credit Preference Shareholders A/c[cite: 15]
options.B: Debit Preference Shareholders A/c, Credit Share Capital A/c
options.C: Debit Bank A/c, Credit Redeemable Preference Share Capital A/c
options.D: Debit CRR A/c, Credit Bank A/c

answer_html: Answer: (A) Redeemable Preference Share Capital A/c is debited and Preference Shareholders A/c is credited[cite: 15].

question_html: If a company has partly paid-up preference shares and wishes to redeem preference shares, what action must be taken first?

options.A: Forfeit the partly paid shares immediately.
options.B: Make the final call and ensure they are fully paid-up before proceeding with redemption[cite: 15].
options.C: Write them off against general reserve.
options.D: Redeem them at a proportionate discount.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Partly paid shares cannot be redeemed; final call must be demanded and received to make them fully paid[cite: 15].

question_html: When preference shares are forfeited due to non-payment of final calls prior to redemption, where is the balance in the Shares Forfeited Account transferred after redemption?

options.A: To Capital Redemption Reserve Account
options.B: To Capital Reserve Account[cite: 15]
options.C: To General Reserve Account
options.D: To Profit and Loss Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) Since forfeited shares are not reissued, the balance in Shares Forfeited Account is transferred to Capital Reserve[cite: 15].

question_html: What is the primary advantage of redeeming preference shares by the issue of fresh equity shares?

options.A: It results in a massive cash inflow from the public.
options.B: There is no cash outflow of money, now or later[cite: 15].
options.C: It increases the fixed dividend burden of the company.
options.D: It avoids all regulatory filings.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Fresh equity issue avoids cash outflow during redemption[cite: 15].

question_html: In calculating the minimum proceeds of a fresh issue of shares for redemption, how is the nominal value of preference shares to be redeemed treated in relation to maximum available divisible profits?

options.A: Minimum proceeds = Nominal value plus premium on redemption.
options.B: Minimum proceeds = Nominal value of preference shares to be redeemed minus maximum amount of reserve and surplus available for redemption[cite: 15].
options.C: Minimum proceeds = Total divisible profits multiplied by 2.
options.D: Minimum proceeds = Paid-up equity capital minus bank balance.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Minimum proceeds = Nominal value of preference shares to be redeemed minus maximum amount of reserve and surplus available for redemption[cite: 15].

question_html: If the calculation of the minimum number of shares to be issued results in a fraction, how should it be approximated?

options.A: Rounded off to the nearest lower integer.
options.B: Approximated to the next higher figure to ensure provisions of Section 55 are not violated[cite: 15].
options.C: Ignored entirely.
options.D: Paid in cash as fractional warrants.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Fractional shares are not permitted, so minimum number of shares must be approximated to the next higher figure[cite: 15].

question_html: What does the term 'Divisible Profit' refer to in the context of company accounts?

options.A: Profits that are legally distributable as dividends to shareholders[cite: 15].
options.B: Capital reserves arising from the forfeiture of shares.
options.C: Profits generated from the revaluation of fixed assets.
options.D: Securities premium collected on share issues.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Profit or a portion of profit that can be otherwise legally distributed as dividend is known as divisible profit[cite: 15].

question_html: What is a primary disadvantage of redeeming preference shares entirely by capitalisation of undistributed divisible profits?

options.A: Dilution of equity shareholding percentage.
options.B: Reduction in liquidity or potential need to sell assets such as investments[cite: 15].
options.C: Mandatory increase in authorized share capital.
options.D: Incurring heavy underwriting commission.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Capitalisation of profits reduces liquidity or may require selling investments to arrange cash[cite: 15].

question_html: When shares are issued at a discount, how is the 'proceeds from fresh issue' interpreted for calculating the transfer to Capital Redemption Reserve?

options.A: Face value of the shares.
options.B: Amount received (i.e., debited to Cash/Bank)[cite: 15].
options.C: Nominal value plus premium.
options.D: Zero proceeds.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Proceeds from fresh issue refer to the amount received (debited to Bank) in case of issue at a discount[cite: 15].

question_html: Hinduja Company Ltd. had 5,000, 8% Redeemable Preference Shares of ₹100 each fully paid, redeemed at par by issuing equity shares of ₹10 each at par. What is the total nominal value of equity shares to be issued?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Total nominal value of preference shares to be redeemed is ₹5,00,000, which must be fully covered by fresh issue or CRR[cite: 15].

question_html: C Ltd. had 10,000, 10% Redeemable Preference Shares of ₹100 each fully paid, redeemed at par by issuing equity shares of ₹10 each at a premium of ₹2 per share. What is the amount credited to Securities Premium?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Face value required = ₹10,00,000. Number of equity shares = ₹10,00,000 / ₹10 = 1,00,000 shares. Premium = 1,00,000 x ₹2 = ₹2,00,000[cite: 15].

question_html: Why might a company issue redeemable preference shares in a dull primary market?

options.A: Because it is a proper and effective way of raising finance when investors are hesitant[cite: 15].
options.B: Because preference shares require no repayment obligation ever.
options.C: Because interest on preference shares is tax-deductible.
options.D: Because they carry mandatory voting rights equal to equity.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Redeemable preference shares provide a proper way of raising finance in a dull primary market[cite: 15].
topic_text: Purpose of Issuing Redeemable Preference Shares

question_html: What condition must be satisfied in a company's Articles of Association before it can issue redeemable preference shares?

options.A: The Articles must explicitly authorize the issue of preference shares[cite: 15].
options.B: The Articles must prohibit equity dividend distribution.
options.C: The Articles must mandate annual redemption.
options.D: No authorization in Articles is required.

answer_html: Answer: (A) A company limited by shares, if so authorised by its Articles, may issue preference shares[cite: 15].

question_html: When preference shares are redeemed partly out of fresh issue and partly out of accumulated profits, what amount is transferred to the Capital Redemption Reserve Account?

options.A: Total nominal value of preference shares redeemed.
options.B: Face value of shares redeemed minus proceeds from fresh issue of shares[cite: 15].
options.C: Total proceeds from fresh issue.
options.D: Premium payable on redemption.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Amount to CRR = Face value of shares redeemed minus proceeds from fresh issue[cite: 15].

question_html: What is the accounting entry for transferring the nominal amount of shares redeemed to the Capital Redemption Reserve Account out of General Reserve?

options.A: General Reserve A/c Dr. To Capital Redemption Reserve A/c[cite: 15]
options.B: Capital Redemption Reserve A/c Dr. To General Reserve A/c
options.C: Preference Shareholders A/c Dr. To Capital Redemption Reserve A/c
options.D: Profit and Loss A/c Dr. To Share Capital A/c

answer_html: Answer: (A) General Reserve A/c is debited and Capital Redemption Reserve A/c is credited[cite: 15].

question_html: Which of the following reserves is NOT available for transfer to Capital Redemption Reserve because it is not a free or divisible profit?

options.A: General Reserve
options.B: Capital Reserve[cite: 15]
options.C: Profit and Loss Account (Credit balance)
options.D: Dividend Equalisation Reserve

answer_html: Answer: (B) Capital reserve and securities premium (not being distributable profits) cannot be utilised for transfer to CRR[cite: 15].
topic_text: Exclusion of Capital Reserve from CRR

question_html: If a company issues fresh shares at a premium for preference share redemption, can the premium collected on the fresh issue be used to finance the face value redemption of preference shares?

options.A: Yes, completely.
options.B: No, premium received on new issue cannot be used to finance the face value redemption of preference shares[cite: 15].
options.C: Yes, up to 50% of the premium amount.
options.D: Only if approved by the Board of Directors.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Premium received on new issue cannot be used to finance the face value redemption; only nominal proceeds count towards replacement[cite: 15].
topic_text: Fresh Issue Premium and Redemption Financing

question_html: What is the accounting entry for writing off the premium payable on redemption of preference shares for a company governed by Section 133?

options.A: Profit and Loss A/c Dr. To Premium on Redemption of Preference Shares A/c[cite: 15]
options.B: Securities Premium A/c Dr. To Premium on Redemption of Preference Shares A/c
options.C: Capital Redemption Reserve A/c Dr. To Premium on Redemption A/c
options.D: Preference Shareholders A/c Dr. To Profit and Loss A/c

answer_html: Answer: (A) Premium on redemption is written off against profits (Profit and Loss A/c)[cite: 15].

question_html: What happens to the percentage of equity shareholding of existing shareholders when preference shares are redeemed entirely by capitalisation of undistributed divisible profits?

options.A: It increases significantly.
options.B: There is no change in the percentage of equity share-holding[cite: 15].
options.C: It decreases due to outside dilution.
options.D: It becomes zero.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Capitalisation of profits leaves the percentage of equity shareholding completely unchanged[cite: 15].

question_html: When calculating the minimum fresh issue of shares to provide funds for redemption, what is compared with funds available for redemption?

options.A: Total authorized share capital
options.B: Amount payable to preference shareholders[cite: 15]
options.C: Total accumulated divisible reserves
options.D: Book value of fixed assets

answer_html: Answer: (B) Amount payable to preference shareholders is compared with available funds to compute the shortfall to be raised by fresh issue[cite: 15].

question_html: What is the legal status of the Capital Redemption Reserve Account in relation to the reduction of share capital?

options.A: It is treated as an intangible asset.
options.B: Provisions of the Act relating to reduction of share capital apply as if CRR were the paid-up share capital of the company[cite: 15].
options.C: It can be distributed freely as interim dividends.
options.D: It can be used to pay director remuneration.

answer_html: Answer: (B) CRR provisions treat the account as if it were the paid-up share capital of the company[cite: 15].

question_html: If a company sells its investments to arrange cash for preference share redemption, how is the loss on sale of investments treated?

options.A: Credited to capital redemption reserve.
options.B: Debited to Profit and Loss Account as a charge[cite: 15].
options.C: Added to the face value of preference shares.
options.D: Ignored for accounting purposes.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Loss on sale of investments is debited to Profit and Loss Account[cite: 15].

question_html: What entry is passed when payment is finally made to preference shareholders upon redemption?

options.A: Preference Shareholders A/c Dr. To Bank A/c[cite: 15]
options.B: Bank A/c Dr. To Preference Shareholders A/c
options.C: Redeemable Preference Share Capital A/c Dr. To Bank A/c
options.D: Preference Shareholders A/c Dr. To Share Capital A/c

answer_html: Answer: (A) Preference Shareholders A/c is debited and Bank A/c is credited upon payment[cite: 15].

question_html: What is the effect on shareholders' funds when preference shares are redeemed out of accumulated profits via Capital Redemption Reserve creation?

options.A: Total shareholders' funds remain unchanged because profits are converted into CRR[cite: 15].
options.B: Total shareholders' funds decrease by the full redemption amount.
options.C: Total shareholders' funds increase due to reserve capitalization.
options.D: Paid-up share capital increases.

answer_html: Answer: (A) There is no net reduction in total shareholders' funds as divisible profits are retained via CRR transfer[cite: 15].

question_html: Which of the following is a disadvantage of redeeming preference shares by issuing fresh equity shares?

options.A: Immediate cash drain from company reserves.
options.B: Dilution of future earnings and potential change in shareholding pattern[cite: 15].
options.C: Mandatory creation of capital redemption reserve for the full amount.
options.D: Prohibition of future bonus issues.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Disadvantages include dilution of future earnings and potential change in shareholding pattern if issued to outsiders[cite: 15].

question_html: If a company has an Investment Allowance Reserve out of which a portion is not free for distribution as dividend, can that restricted portion be used for transfer to Capital Redemption Reserve?

options.A: Yes, all statutory reserves are divisible.
options.B: No, only free/divisible reserves can be used to create CRR[cite: 15].
options.C: Yes, with court permission.
options.D: Only if securities premium is exhausted first.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Non-free reserves (like restricted portions of allowance reserves) cannot be used for CRR[cite: 15].

question_html: What is the definition of 'Redemption' in corporate finance?

options.A: The process of issuing new equity shares at a premium.
options.B: The process of repaying an obligation at prearranged amounts and timings[cite: 15].
options.C: The capitalization of general reserves into bonus shares.
options.D: The forfeiture of partly paid shares due to unpaid calls.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Redemption is the process of repaying an obligation at prearranged amounts and timings[cite: 15].

question_html: When preference shares are redeemed at a premium, what is the accounting entry for transferring the amount payable (including premium) to the Preference Shareholders Account?

options.A: Redeemable Preference Share Capital A/c Dr., Premium on Redemption of Preference Shares A/c Dr. To Preference Shareholders A/c[cite: 15]
options.B: Preference Shareholders A/c Dr. To Share Capital A/c, To Securities Premium A/c
options.C: Bank A/c Dr. To Preference Shareholders A/c
options.D: CRR A/c Dr. To Preference Shareholders A/c

answer_html: Answer: (A) Preference Share Capital and Premium on Redemption are debited, and Preference Shareholders A/c is credited[cite: 15].
topic_text: Accounting Entry for Redemption at Premium

question_html: Why might a company choose to redeem preference shares when there is a surplus of capital?

options.A: Because surplus funds cannot be utilized effectively for profitable use in the business[cite: 15].
options.B: To increase its annual fixed dividend burden.
options.C: To comply with mandatory RBI guidelines for debt reduction.
options.D: To avoid paying income tax on profits.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Preference shares may be redeemed when there is surplus capital that cannot be utilized for profitable use[cite: 15].
topic_text: Purpose of Redemption on Capital Surplus

question_html: In calculating the proceeds of a fresh issue of shares, are amounts received towards share premium included as 'proceeds' for capital replacement under Section 55?

options.A: Yes, share premium forms part of fresh issue proceeds.
options.B: No, share premium is excluded because premium cannot be used to finance face value redemption[cite: 15].
options.C: Yes, if approved by auditors.
options.D: Only for unlisted private companies.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Premium received is credited to Securities Premium and is not regarded as proceeds for CRR calculation purposes[cite: 15].
topic_text: Exclusion of Premium from Fresh Issue Proceeds

question_html: What is the nature of the Capital Redemption Reserve Account in the balance sheet?

options.A: Current Liability
options.B: Reserve and Surplus under Shareholders' Funds[cite: 15]
options.C: Non-current Asset
options.D: Contingent Liability

answer_html: Answer: (B) Capital Redemption Reserve is presented under Reserves and Surplus within Shareholders' Funds[cite: 15].

question_html: If a company decides to retain a specified minimum balance in its General Reserve that cannot be utilized under any circumstances, how does this affect the calculation of maximum divisible profits available for preference share redemption?

options.A: The restricted retention amount must be deducted from the total general reserve balance[cite: 15].
options.B: It is added to the redemption proceeds.
options.C: It has no impact on available reserves.
options.D: It doubles the capital redemption reserve requirement.

answer_html: Answer: (A) The restricted retention amount is excluded, leaving only the net available general reserve for redemption[cite: 15].

question_html: What entry is passed when application money is received for fresh equity shares issued for preference share redemption?

options.A: Bank A/c Dr. To Equity Share Application A/c[cite: 15]
options.B: Equity Share Application A/c Dr. To Bank A/c
options.C: Share Capital A/c Dr. To Bank A/c
options.D: Preference Shareholders A/c Dr. To Bank A/c

answer_html: Answer: (A) Bank A/c is debited and Equity Share Application A/c is credited upon receipt of application money[cite: 15].

question_html: What amount of fresh issue proceeds is considered when fresh shares are issued in installments (e.g., application and allotment) but the final call is due after the redemption date?

options.A: Total face value of shares issued regardless of call status.
options.B: Only the amount received (called up and paid up) on fresh issue of shares till the date of redemption[cite: 15].
options.C: Zero proceeds until all calls are fully collected.
options.D: Face value plus premium due.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Amount received (excluding premium) on fresh issue of shares till the date of redemption should be considered for calculation of proceeds[cite: 15].

question_html: Can a company adjust the premium payable on redemption of preference shares against its Capital Reserve Account?

options.A: Yes, capital reserves are specifically meant for redemption premiums.
options.B: No, capital reserves are not divisible profits and cannot be used for writing off redemption premiums[cite: 15].
options.C: Yes, with special resolution approval.
options.D: Only if securities premium is unavailable.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Capital reserves are non-distributable and cannot be used to write off redemption premiums[cite: 15].

question_html: If the whereabouts of the holders of certain fully paid preference shares are unknown at the time of redemption, how is the redemption accounted for?

options.A: Those shares are cancelled without payment obligation.
options.B: Redemption is executed for known shareholders, while amounts due for unknown holders are transferred or handled as per statutory unclaimed liability rules[cite: 15].
options.C: The entire redemption process is legally stayed by the court.
options.D: The shares are converted into equity.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Redemption proceeds for shares whose holders' whereabouts are unknown are accounted for while paying active claimants[cite: 15].
